meta.title: TimeCop: The Missing Grail
meta.notes: 30-section sample with good/bad/special endings that loop back to start.
meta.blurb: A Mastermind time-criminal is stealing sacred artifacts. Your first mission: recover the Holy Grail before history forgets it ever existed.

S01.text:
The briefing room smells like burnt coffee and recycled air.

Your supervisor doesn’t waste time. A timeline grid blooms across the wall—bright threads, clean intersections, the kind of order people assume history has.

Then the grid flickers. Small punctures. Missing nodes. Not explosions—quiet absences.

“Mastermind,” your supervisor says. “Career thief. Not here to kill anyone. Here to steal what makes people *believe*.”

A file hangs at the center of the screen.

THE HOLY GRAIL — STATUS: UNKNOWN.

A relic like that isn’t just gold and legend. It’s a foundation stone. Remove it, and whole centuries start to feel different.

You’re new, but you’re not green. You know what happens when people stop trusting the story the world tells them.


CHOICES

REVIEW THE CASE FILE
You slow down long enough to see how the Mastermind moves, and what they’ve hit before.

SUIT UP AND JUMP
You go now, betting speed beats preparation.

S02.text:
The case file is a list of things that should not be missing.

A crown that vanishes from a coronation painting. A page ripped out of a treaty that still gets signed. A prototype that never makes it into a workshop.

The pattern is obvious once you see it: the Mastermind steals symbols that hold history together. Not weapons—anchors.

Your supervisor scrolls to a note in red: “They leave decoys. They like to watch us chase the wrong shadow.”

One more page is tagged with higher clearance. You don’t *have* to open it.

But you do.

It’s a grainy image of a jump-signature waveform—two peaks instead of one. Hesitation, like the thief is stepping across a crack in reality and trying not to fall.

Stolen stabilizer tech. Old. Dangerous.

If they jump again, they might not land where they intend.


CHOICES

RUN TEMPORAL FORENSICS
You take thirty seconds to lock onto the Mastermind’s signature, so you can track them mid-flight.

DEPLOY ANYWAY
You jump now, and accept that you may be running blind.

S03.text:
The jump is never graceful.

The agency’s clean lights smear into a tunnel of motion. Your stomach lifts, your ears pop, and for a heartbeat you feel like a photograph being peeled off a page.

Then mud hits your boots.

Rain. Torchlight. Stone walls rising out of the storm.

A monastery sits on a hill like it’s been waiting for centuries—and maybe it has.

Your wrist unit pings once: temporal residue, fresh. Whoever came through, they did it recently.

You pull your coat tighter and let your eyes do what they were trained to do: look for what doesn’t belong.

A modern scuff in ancient mud.

A handprint where no one would touch.

A whisper of ozone that doesn’t match the weather.


CHOICES

ENTER THE MONASTERY
You go straight in. Faster. Riskier. You might be seen.

SCOUT THE PERIMETER
You circle first. The Mastermind had to enter somewhere, and thieves always leave a trail.

S04.text:
Forensics is boring until it saves your life.

You overlay the Mastermind’s waveform against the current era. The double-peak signature stands out like a stutter in music.

“Stabilizer is degrading,” the lab tech says. “They can’t keep doing this. Each jump is rougher than the last.”

Rough jumps mean mistakes.

Mistakes mean windows.

You mark the most likely landing points—places where a relic like the Grail would be whispered about, hidden, guarded.

The monastery on the hill lights up as a probability spike.

You don’t feel triumphant. You feel the calm that comes right before things go wrong.

Because if the Mastermind is desperate, they might do something stupid.

And stupid in time travel doesn’t just get people killed.

It gets *forgotten*.


CHOICES

JUMP WITH TRACKING ACTIVE
You go now, tuned to their signature.

CALL FOR BACKUP
You request support and risk arriving late.

S05.text:
Inside the monastery, the air is warm and thick with candle smoke.

A monk meets you with wary eyes. You can’t show him a badge that means anything here, so you show him urgency instead.

He leads you down stone halls. Whispers follow.

“A stranger came,” a voice murmurs.

“Light in the corridor,” another says.

“Like a star fell inside,” someone else insists.

At the reliquary door, the monk stops.

The iron latch is bent outward.

Not forced in.

Forced *open*.

You step through and feel your stomach drop.

The pedestal is bare.

The place where history says the Grail should be… is empty.


CHOICES

SEARCH THE RELIQUARY
You look for residue, a hidden compartment, anything the thief overlooked.

QUESTION THE WITNESSES
You gather details: voice, height, direction, timing. Thieves hate questions.

S06.text:
Mud is honest.

You circle the outer wall, keeping low, scanning for anything that doesn’t match the era.

There—a set of boot prints with tread too sharp, too uniform.

Someone climbed here fast.

You follow the prints to a spot where stone is scraped clean. A handhold. A jump point.

Nearby, a faint scorch mark—small, like a portable device venting heat.

The Mastermind didn’t stroll in.

They slipped.

They were in a hurry.

That’s good for you.

Hurried thieves make greedy choices.


CHOICES

FOLLOW THE TRAIL
You keep tracking along the mud line toward where they exited.

RETURN INSIDE
You go back through the monastery to confirm the Grail is truly gone.

S07.text:
You call for backup.

A sensible move. A professional move.

Time doesn’t care.

Your wrist unit pulses—one sharp spike, then silence.

The Mastermind jumped.

You feel the moment like a door slamming in another room.

Backup arrives two minutes later. Too clean. Too calm. Too late.

They look at you like you’re supposed to say something inspiring.

But you’re thinking of the double-peak signature.

Unstable.

Desperate.

And now moving.


CHOICES

PURSUE THROUGH TIME
You jump after the spike. You may be walking into a trap.

STAND DOWN
You accept failure. You write the report. You live with it.

S08.text:
You kneel by the pedestal.

Nothing obvious. No secret latch. No false bottom.

But the air tastes wrong—like metal and lightning.

Temporal residue.

Fresh.

The Mastermind didn’t just pick up the Grail. They *opened* something to take it.

A small smear of soot marks the stone rim, as if a device kissed it for half a second.

You trace the mark with a gloved finger.

Your wrist unit chirps.

A directional ping.

They left a wake.

If you move fast, you can still catch the ripple before it fades.


CHOICES

FOLLOW THE RESIDUE
You step into pursuit while the trail is still warm.

STOP AND LISTEN
You slow down and let the monastery tell you what it saw.

S09.text:
The monks don’t have your words, but they have eyes.

They describe the thief as calm, almost respectful. No shouting. No panic.

A stranger who looked at the relic like it was a memory.

One monk mentions something odd: the thief said, softly, before vanishing—

“People would kill for hope. History should share it.”

That’s not greed.

That’s a story the thief tells themselves.

And stories are dangerous.

Because the wrong story can justify anything.


CHOICES

INTERCEPT THE NEXT JUMP
You use the residue trail to catch them mid-flight.

SEAL THE ERA
You contain the damage and accept you may never recover the Grail.

S10.text:
The trail leads away from the monastery into a narrow path cut through trees.

Rain turns everything into the same color, but your scanner sees what your eyes can’t.

A thin thread of temporal distortion—like heat shimmer, except cold.

It pulls you toward a clearing.

And in that clearing:

A ring of scorched earth.

A jump site.

The Mastermind didn’t leave quietly.

They left in a hurry.

You step closer, and the air prickles.

Your unit buzzes.

A residual echo plays, like a recording on a loop: a figure lifting a cup-shaped relic, then turning as if they *heard you coming*.


CHOICES

TRIGGER A TRACE BEACON
You tag the jump site so you can follow their next tear.

JUMP THROUGH THE ECHO
You dive into the unstable corridor now, before it collapses.

S11.text:
You jump after the spike.

The corridor is wrong. Too jagged. Too loud.

You land hard in a place that isn’t quite a place—half formed, like the universe didn’t finish loading it.

Someone is waiting.

Not the Mastermind.

A hired runner from the future, face masked, weapon cheap and loud.

They don’t say anything.

They just raise the gun.

You don’t have time to wonder why the Mastermind sent them.

You have time to move.


CHOICES

TAKE COVER AND DISARM
You survive first. Ask questions later.

CHARGE AND END IT
You go aggressive. Faster, riskier, messier.

S12.text:
Sealing an era is a polite way of saying you’re cleaning up someone else’s mess.

You mark the monastery timeline with stabilization protocols.

The missing Grail becomes a controlled absence—a patch on the story.

People will still speak of it.

They’ll just speak differently.

You can feel it already: the way meaning shifts when the object is gone.

Your supervisor will call it a partial success.

You’ll call it a loss that doesn’t bleed.

But it still bleeds.

Just slow.


CHOICES

FILE THE REPORT
You accept the damage and return to the agency.

CHANGE YOUR MIND
You pursue anyway. You refuse to leave history wounded.

S13.text:
You plant the beacon.

A tiny device, smaller than a coin, that clings to the edge of a tear in reality and listens for the next one.

It’s not glamorous.

It’s effective.

Your wrist unit ticks.

One second.

Two.

Then a soft chime.

The Mastermind’s signature is back—double peak, unstable, close.

Your beacon caught it.

A new destination bleeds into your display.

A market town.

Busy streets.

Too many innocents.

Perfect cover for a thief.


CHOICES

JUMP TO THE MARKET
You take the route with the highest chance of contact.

WAIT AND TRIANGULATE
You refine the lock for a cleaner jump—at the cost of time.

S14.text:
You jump through the echo before it can fade.

The corridor snaps shut behind you like a trap.

You land in a medieval market town, rain replaced by damp fog and the stink of animals.

People push past you. Traders shout. Children run.

And somewhere in the noise, your unit pings.

The Grail is close.

Too close.

You can almost feel its weight in the air.

But you can’t draw a weapon here.

Not without becoming the monster in everyone’s story.


CHOICES

BLEND INTO THE CROWD
You hide your urgency and hunt like a shadow.

HEAD FOR HIGH GROUND
You get a vantage and risk losing the trail in the crowd.

S15.text:
You dive behind a half-formed stone pillar.

The runner fires twice. The shots crack like thunder in a world that doesn’t like loud noises.

You slide, grab their wrist, twist.

The gun clatters.

They panic.

You see it in their eyes: they don’t want to die in a place that might not even exist tomorrow.

You pin them and speak low.

“Where’s the Mastermind?”

They laugh once—short, bitter.

“Everywhere.”

And then they bite down on something.

Their body goes limp.

Self-erase capsule.

Cheap insurance.


CHOICES

FOLLOW THE RESIDUAL SIGNATURE
You use the runner’s fading waveform to find the Mastermind.

RETREAT TO STABILITY
You leave before the corridor collapses on you.

S16.text:
You rush them.

Your shoulder clips the weapon as it fires.

Pain blooms—hot, immediate, real.

The runner stumbles back, startled you’re still standing.

You grab their mask, yank.

They’re young.

Too young to be here.

Their eyes flick to your bleeding side, and you realize what they were hired to do: delay you. Not kill you.

They smile like they know something.

“Too late,” they whisper.

And then they vanish—jump device, cheap and violent.

Your wound pulses.

Your unit screams: corridor collapse imminent.


CHOICES

PUSH THROUGH THE PAIN
You pursue while you still can.

FALL BACK AND PATCH UP
You survive now and risk losing them.

S17.text:
The market town is alive with noise.

You step out of the jump with your coat pulled tight and your face neutral.

You scan hands.

You scan pockets.

You scan eyes.

Thieves always look like they’re counting.

Your unit pings.

Close.

Then closer.

A figure slips between stalls—hood up, pace unhurried.

They aren’t running.

They’re *sure*.

And certainty is the most dangerous thing a criminal can carry.


CHOICES

FOLLOW AT A DISTANCE
You stay back and wait for a cleaner moment.

CUT THEM OFF
You move fast and try to corner them before they vanish again.

S18.text:
You refine your lock.

It’s clean work. Precise work.

By the time you jump, you arrive smoothly—almost like you belonged here.

But the market is already shifting.

The figure you expected is gone.

The trail is weaker.

And you feel it: the Mastermind wants you just behind them.

Wants you tired.

Wants you reaching.

You don’t know why yet.

You just know it’s true.


CHOICES

SEARCH FOR THE TRAIL
You hunt the residue like a bloodhound.

ASK THE WRONG QUESTIONS
You use your badge in a world that doesn’t understand it—and hope fear does the rest.

S19.text:
You trail them through the crowd.

They never look back.

They don’t need to.

They know you’re there.

They drift toward a quiet side street where the noise dies and the air smells like wet stone. A place where a jump could happen without witnesses.

The figure pauses at a door.

Not a shop.

Not a home.

A storage building with a weak lock.

They slip inside.

You wait three seconds.

Then follow.


CHOICES

ENTER QUIETLY
You take the careful approach.

KICK THE DOOR
You go loud and fast, betting surprise beats subtlety.

S20.text:
You find the residue again—thin, but real.

It drifts toward the river road, away from the market.

Your unit pings a second signature too.

Not the Mastermind.

A stabilizer echo.

Old tech.

Failing.

They can’t keep doing this.

Which means they’re heading somewhere to finish the job.

Somewhere they can’t risk leaving without the Grail.

You follow the thread until the town thins.

Until the fog opens.

Until you see a lone figure by the river, hood up, holding something close to their chest.


CHOICES

APPROACH AND TALK
You risk conversation to learn what they want.

TAKE THE SHOT
You go for the arrest immediately.

S21.text:
You retreat to a stable pocket of time.

You press gauze to your side, breathe through the sting, and watch your unit settle.

It’s the right call.

But it feels like surrender.

Your supervisor’s voice crackles in your earpiece: “Status?”

You could lie.

You could tell the truth.

Either way, the Mastermind is moving.

And the longer you wait, the more the story reshapes around the missing Grail.


CHOICES

RETURN TO THE HUNT
You go back in before you’re fully ready.

REPORT AND STAND DOWN
You choose survival and accept the loss.

S22.text:
You cut them off in the street.

They stop without surprise.

Up close, you see details you didn’t expect: clean hands, calm eyes, no obvious weapon.

Just a device strapped to the wrist.

And under the cloak, the faint outline of something cup-shaped.

The Grail.

Their mouth curves like they’ve been waiting for you.

“TimeCop,” they say.

You didn’t tell them your title.

Which means they’ve done their homework.

Or they’ve met your kind before.


CHOICES

DEMAND THE RELIC
You keep it simple: give it back.

STALL FOR A CLEAN ARREST
You talk, you keep them calm, you wait for an opening.

S23.text:
You flash a badge no one understands.

People stare.

You raise your voice.

People back away.

Fear works, but it leaves stains.

A woman clutches a child and runs.

A merchant pulls a knife.

And the Mastermind—somewhere in the shifting crowd—moves like water.

Your unit pings wildly.

Then stops.

The signature is gone.

You pushed the world too hard.

You made yourself the story.

And the thief slipped away.


CHOICES

CHASE THE LAST PING
You gamble on instinct.

ACCEPT FAILURE
You end it here and live with what you did.

S24.text:
Inside the storage building, it’s dark and damp.

The Mastermind stands near the back wall, the Grail cradled like it’s fragile.

They don’t run.

They don’t even flinch.

They just look at you with the calm of someone who believes they’re right.

“I don’t steal,” they say.

“I recover.”

You hear the jump-device hum.

It’s strained.

Overworked.

And you realize something: they’re not planning to keep the Grail here.

They’re planning to take it somewhere you can’t easily follow.


CHOICES

ARREST THEM NOW
You go hands-on. End it.

ASK WHY THE GRAIL
You risk conversation to find leverage.

S25.text:
You kick the door.

Wood splinters.

The Mastermind turns, surprised for the first time.

The Grail slips—almost falls.

You lunge.

They lunge.

For half a second, you both hold it.

The air cracks.

Your unit screams.

And suddenly you understand: the Grail isn’t just symbolic.

It’s resonant.

A stabilizing anchor.

Touching it during a jump could rewrite the rules.

They wrench it free.

“Careful,” they say.

And the jump-device flares.


CHOICES

DIVE WITH THEM
You grab on and ride the jump.

LET THEM GO
You refuse to risk tearing the timeline apart.

S26.text:
You talk.

It feels wrong, letting a thief speak. But you’ve learned that the best criminals don’t hide behind silence—they hide behind meaning.

“The Grail,” you say. “Why that?”

Their eyes flick to the cup.

“Because it changes what people do when they believe,” they answer.

“You protect history. But whose version?”

They step closer. Not threatening. Intimate, like they want you to share a secret.

“I can show you,” they say. “A future where hope isn’t rationed.”

The jump-device whines.

They’re offering you a door.

And every door has a price.


CHOICES

REFUSE AND ARREST
You reject the philosophy and do your job.

HEAR THE OFFER
You let them show you what they mean.

S27.text:
You move.

Fast. Professional.

The Mastermind reacts, but not fast enough.

Your cuff-device snaps onto their wrist. The jump-tech sputters.

For a heartbeat, you think it’s over.

Then the double-peak signature spikes.

Their stabilizer fails.

Reality shudders.

The Mastermind’s face twists—not fear, not anger—regret.

“Not like this,” they whisper.

The corridor opens behind them like a mouth.

You have the Grail in reach.

But the corridor is pulling.

And the market outside is full of people.


CHOICES

SECURE THE GRAIL
You prioritize the relic and let the Mastermind fall.

SAVE THE CROWD
You stabilize the tear to protect civilians—at the cost of pursuit.

S28.text:
You dive with them.

The jump hits like a punch.

You see flashes: a cathedral that hasn’t been built yet, a museum that’s already burned down, a vault door with your agency’s seal.

The Mastermind is dragging the Grail through time like a key.

Your grip slips.

Your unit overloads.

And for the first time, you feel what it’s like to be out of control in history’s bloodstream.

You slam into a clean white room.

Not medieval.

Not modern.

Agency.

But wrong.

Everything is familiar—just slightly off.

The Mastermind looks almost relieved.

“We made it,” they say.


CHOICES

CALL FOR HELP
You alert the agency—even if you’re not sure it’s your agency.

TAKE THE GRAIL AND RUN
You grab the relic and flee before the Mastermind can lock the door behind you.

S29.text:
They show you.

Not with a speech.

With a window.

The Mastermind triggers the Grail’s resonance and the room fills with overlapping futures—brief, sharp, painful.

A city where medicine is free.

A century where no one kneels to kings.

A world where the Grail never became a myth because it was shared openly.

Then you see the cost.

Threads snapping.

People disappearing from photographs.

A child crying at an empty chair because someone who should exist… doesn’t.

The Mastermind watches your face.

“Hope,” they say softly. “Is always paid for.”


CHOICES

RETURN THE GRAIL TO HISTORY
You choose stability over temptation.

KEEP IT FOR THE AGENCY
You choose control—your agency’s control.

S30.text:
You get the Grail back to where it belongs.

The moment you set it down, the world exhales.

The noise in your unit settles.

The air stops prickling.

History clicks back into alignment like a lock finding its key.

You don’t feel heroic.

You feel tired.

Because you can’t shake the thought that the Mastermind wasn’t wrong about everything.

And that’s the part that will follow you home.


CHOICES

FILE IT AS A WIN
You close the case and accept that you’ll never know what might have been.

OPEN A QUIET INVESTIGATION
You keep digging. Who taught the Mastermind to use the Grail like a key?

END_GOOD.text:
GOOD ENDING — HISTORY HOLDS

The Holy Grail returns to its proper place in the story.

The timeline stabilizes. Reports are filed. The monastery forgets the details, but keeps the feeling: something sacred was almost taken.

Your supervisor signs off with a curt nod.

“Clean work,” they say.

You go back to your quarters and stare at the ceiling.

Because you keep hearing the Mastermind’s question:

Whose version of history are you protecting?


CHOICES

RETURN TO START
You begin again—because history always does.

END_BAD.text:
BAD ENDING — THE STORY THINS

The Grail remains missing.

Nothing explodes. No obvious paradox tears the sky.

It’s worse than that.

Over months, you notice it: old paintings look slightly wrong. Stories people tell at night lose their warmth. Certain songs stop being written.

History survives.

But it feels… less certain.

You file the report and realize no one wants to read it.

Because admitting a symbol is gone means admitting the world can be rewritten by anyone with enough nerve.


CHOICES

RETURN TO START
You try again. Different choices. Different cost.

END_SPECIAL.text:
SPECIAL ENDING — YOU BECOME THE QUESTION

The Grail ends up in a place history will never see.

A vault.

A lab.

A hand that isn’t supposed to hold it.

Maybe it’s your agency’s containment.

Maybe it’s something pretending to be.

Either way, the Mastermind’s smile lingers in your mind like a bruise.

Because now you understand the real threat.

It wasn’t the thief.

It was the idea that history can be *managed*.

And you’re part of that system.

A message appears on your wrist unit—no sender, no time stamp:

“Welcome to the long game.”


CHOICES

RETURN TO START
You go back to the beginning—because now you know what to look for.
